core.title: Reference train prerequisites in the train URN shape
core.given: A train's plan artifact exists or is being authored, edited, reviewed or validated, with or without existing dependency entries
core.when: The planner writes, changes or checks that train's dependencies
core.then: Every entry in the train's dependencies must be a reference to a prerequisite train, written in the train URN shape given by the profile.
prefer: Foundation (commons) trains often precede the trains that build on them; order them first when that applies — a frequent pattern, not an unconditional requirement.
avoid: A data-flow consumer train that does not depend on the train producing the data it consumes — consumers must depend on producers.
Circular dependencies between trains — direct, transitive, or a train listing itself — are forbidden.
Free-text, bare-id or references to finer-grained plan artifacts (such as wagons) in the dependencies list instead of a train reference in the train URN shape.
Reversing direction: making a producer depend on its consumer.
core.why: A dependency is a prerequisite train reference; one uniform train reference shape lets tooling resolve ordering, consumers need their producers first, and a cycle makes the trains impossible to sequence.
evidence: Every entry in each train's dependencies matches the profile's train URN shape and resolves to an existing train.
A graph walk over all train dependencies (including self-edges) finds no cycle.
Each consumer train lists the train producing its consumed data among its dependencies; no producer depends on its consumer.
verification: Treat every dependency entry as a prerequisite-train reference and validate it against the profile's train URN shape; an entry that does not match, or does not resolve to an existing train, is a violation.
Validate existing entries on every train, not only on trains changed in the current edit; a train referencing itself is a cycle of length one.

The reference-shape check and the whole-graph cycle walk (self-edges included) are mechanical; the consumer-depends-on-producer (data-flow) check is llm_judged unless the stack's plan data records train-level produce/consume relationships.

values: train dependency list added or edited
dependency reference not matching the train reference shape
consumer train missing dependency on its producer train

fires: Planner authors a new train that needs another train's outputs or foundation first
Planner edits the dependencies list of an existing train
Planner adds or edits a train that consumes data produced by another train
Planner reviews or validates existing train specs, including ones whose dependencies list contains malformed references, a self-reference, or a cycle
Planner edits any part of a train spec whose existing dependencies violate the reference shape or form a cycle
doesNotFire: Editing a wagon's internal acceptances or WMBTs without touching or reviewing any train spec
Authoring documentation or plans that do not define, edit or validate train specs

profileRequirements.meaning: The URN shape every prerequisite-train reference must match — the core's 'train URN shape' in then, avoid, evidence and the check.
The concrete plan-artifact kinds this rule fires on: the kind that defines a train and the registry kind that lists trains.

neutralityNotes: Trains, wagons and WMBTs are ATDD plan-artifact vocabulary present in the closed profile vocabulary (urn.train, urn.wagon, urn.wmbt, layout.wagon_dir), so the core uses them rather than code roles; no stack, runtime, framework, language, package manager, file suffix or path is named. The only genuinely stack-specific datum is the concrete reference form train:{train_id} / ^train:[0-9]{2}-[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$, which becomes profile data (urn.train); a stack with a different train URN shape realizes the identical obligation with its own value. The two concrete source examples (verifier_detail[1], verifier_detail[2]) stay Bun-only under the reference-example policy. 'unless' is empty in bun.json and remains empty in the core. bun.json declares no per-rule severity or disposition, so none was invented; the llm_judged status of the consumer→producer check and the validate-every-train scope are kept in core.verification.
